words.meaning: to prevent or delay something by acting ahead of time
words.example: The team published a clear timeline to forestall confusion about the rollout.

words.meaning: difficult to manage because of its size, complexity, or awkwardness
words.example: The spreadsheet became unwieldy after every department added its own tracking columns.

words.meaning: matching something else in size, degree, or importance
words.example: The role carries more responsibility, so the salary should be commensurate with it.

words.meaning: to assign someone or something to a less important position or role
words.example: We should not relegate customer feedback to a footnote in the planning process.

words.meaning: quick and not thorough enough to consider all the details
words.example: A cursory review missed the billing error hidden near the end of the contract.

phrases.meaning: to appear unexpectedly or seem unrelated to what was happening
phrases.example: The request to change vendors came out of left field during the budget meeting.

phrases.meaning: to feel slightly sick or unwell
phrases.example: I am a little under the weather, so I will join the meeting from home.

phrases.meaning: to speak or act quickly without careful preparation
phrases.example: I do not want to shoot from the hip, so let me check the numbers first.

phrases.meaning: to use personal influence or connections to make something happen
phrases.example: She pulled some strings and got us a reservation at the fully booked restaurant.

phrases.meaning: to accept responsibility and take action when needed
phrases.example: When the project lead got sick, Maya stepped up to the plate and ran the presentation.
